Record a recode as a manifest that can be signed and verified later

Source: R/categorical_guard.R
rcdmnf.Rd

Builds a record of a recode that a later reader can check: the mapping and its SHA-256, the counts per label before and after, the results of the before/after cross-tabulation check and (when given) of the match against published counts, a UTC timestamp, and, with a key, a signature over the whole record. Write it to disk with wrrcdmnf and re-check it with vrfrcdmnf, so anyone can confirm which labels went where and that nothing was changed afterwards.

Usage

rcdmnf(orig, recd, map, pub = NULL, key = NULL, ctx = NULL)

Arguments

orig, recd

Vectors of the same length: the values before and after the recode.

map

Named character vector, old = new: the mapping that was applied.

pub

Optional named numeric vector of published counts per recoded label, default NULL (no check).

key

Optional signing key, default NULL (unsigned): a key from pqckg or fipskg. When given the manifest carries a signature and the public key.

ctx

Optional character string, default NULL: free text such as the dataset, table and analyst. Only the first element is kept.

Value

A list of class bricklayer_recode_manifest with these elements:

  • context;

  • created (ISO 8601 UTC time);

  • mapping (list) and mapping_sha256;

  • n (number of rows) and n_missing;

  • counts_before and counts_after (named lists of counts);

  • checks, a list: crosstab_is_function, missingness_unchanged and matches_published;

  • published (list or NULL);

  • body_sha256;

  • with a key, signature and public_key.

Details

The function first runs vrfrcd, as vrfrcd(original, recoded, mapping). When pub is given it then runs vrfmrg, as vrfmrg(recoded, published), with the default strict = TRUE. Either check failing is an error, so a manifest is only produced for a recode that passed. For that reason checks$matches_published is TRUE or NA (no published counts), never FALSE.

body_sha256 is csha256 of the canonical JSON of every other field. With a key, cpssign signs that hash and the manifest also stores the public key: a bricklayer_signing_key from pqckg (XMSS, which consumes one one-time leaf per signature) or a key from fipskg (ML-DSA or SLH-DSA). Nothing is written to disk.

Examples

x <- c("W", "B", "W", "I")
map <- c(W = "White", B = "Black", I = "Indigenous")
y <- grdrcd(x, map)
m <- rcdmnf(x, y, map,
  pub = c(White = 2, Black = 1, Indigenous = 1),
  ctx = "example survey, race item"
)
m$checks
#> $crosstab_is_function
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $missingness_unchanged
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $matches_published
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
m$counts_after
#> $Black
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $Indigenous
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $White
#> [1] 2
#> 

# signed with an ML-DSA key
k <- fipskg(seed = as.raw(1:32))
ms <- rcdmnf(x, y, map, key = k)
names(ms)
#>  [1] "context"        "created"        "mapping"        "mapping_sha256"
#>  [5] "n"              "n_missing"      "counts_before"  "counts_after"  
#>  [9] "checks"         "published"      "body_sha256"    "signature"     
#> [13] "public_key"    

# a recode that does not match the published counts is refused
try(rcdmnf(x, y, map, pub = c(White = 1, Black = 2, Indigenous = 1)))
#> Error : vrfmrg: recoded counts do not match the published counts. White: observed 2, published 1; Black: observed 1, published 2; Indigenous: observed 1, published 1. The observed counts match the published ones if the labels are permuted (White -> Black, Black -> White): the labels are attached to the wrong groups.
